title: An Examination and Critique of Subjective Methods to Determine Exercise Intensity: The Talk Test, Feeling Scale, and Rating of Perceived Exertion
authors: Bok D, Rakovac M, Foster C
population: Review of reliability and construct validity of the talk test, Feeling Scale and RPE for delineating ventilatory threshold and respiratory compensation threshold
findings: The talk test and RPE appear to be valid measures of both the ventilatory threshold (VT) and the respiratory compensation threshold (RCP).
Equivocal talk-test stage, RPE of 10-11 and Feeling Scale ratings between +1 and +3 reflect VT.
Negative talk-test stage, RPE of 13-15 and Feeling Scale ratings around 0 reflect RCP.

Talk test and RPE can elicit responses consistent with moderate, heavy and severe domains; physiological responses to constant Feeling Scale ratings vary widely around VT and are not considered effective for demarcating moderate to heavy.
limitations: Narrative review; the abstract does not name the RPE scale (10-11 and 13-15 are consistent with the Borg 6-20 scale, an inference); talk-test studies were mostly not in runners.
implications: When no HR or pace threshold data exist, use perceived-effort anchors: RPE about 10-11 (Borg 6-20) and the equivocal talk-test stage mark VT1; RPE 13-15 and a negative talk test mark the RCP/VT2 region.
Do not use the Feeling Scale to set the upper threshold boundary; use it only as a secondary comfort cue.
Do not convert these values to a 0-10 RPE scale without a separate source.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (vol 52 pp 2085-2109). Abstract confirms values. Feeling Scale statement tightened to the abstract's wording.
